claims.text: The coupled tribo-corrosion response in high-entropy alloys is governed by synergy between mechanical wear and electrochemical activity.
Wear-induced surface roughness enhances localized corrosion by exposing fresh, reactive surfaces.
Mechanical material removal enhances localized corrosion by disrupting passive oxide layers.
The initial high-entropy alloy has a stable passive oxide layer in the corrosive environment.
Surface roughness and passive-oxide integrity mediate the tribo-corrosion response.
Mechanical wear disrupts the passive oxide layer.
Mechanical wear increases surface roughness and exposes fresh, reactive alloy material to the corrosive environment.
Exposure of fresh, reactive alloy material accelerates localized corrosion.
Accelerated corrosion weakens the material and thereby exacerbates wear.
Wear-enhanced corrosion and corrosion-enhanced wear form a positive feedback loop.
Total degradation during simultaneous tribo-corrosion will exceed the sum of degradation measured under wear-only and corrosion-only conditions.
The wear component will increase under coupled conditions because corrosion weakens the material.
The corrosion component will increase under coupled conditions because wear exposes fresh surfaces.
The proposed mechanism should apply to passivating high-entropy alloys in aqueous environments where wear and corrosion are both active.
The proposed mechanism may fail in non-aqueous environments.
The proposed mechanism may fail for alloys without a significant passive oxide layer.
The magnitude of wear-corrosion synergy and the relative contributions of roughness and oxide disruption are not well quantified.
